message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is slightly below the normal‑pressure freezing point (0 °C) because the solid–liquid equilibrium line for water slopes downward with increasing pressure (water expands when it freezes). Thus, at lower pressures the freezing point rises a bit, and at 10 kPa it is about –2 °C.
